gap: No result ChatGPT got works out that, once a phone is on the second USB-C port, the UGREEN Nexode 65W travel and both Verbatim 65W 3-port chargers all give the laptop the same 45 W (69% of 65 W). So power can't separate them, and weight is the figure that does: Verbatim 30290 is 1.55 g/W, Verbatim 32201 is 1.62 g/W, and the UGREEN is 2.1 or 5.2 g/W depending on which of its two published weights is right.
standout_why: Rivals checked: SmartGadgetKit's UGREEN review (cited) lists 340 g and the 45 + 20 W split for the UGREEN only. Best Batteries' review (cited) lists 135 g, 45 + 20 W and 91.6% efficiency for the UGREEN only. MobilePlusTech gives no weights or prices and computes no derived figure; it gives a split for the UGREEN alone. None of them compares laptop watts with a phone attached across products, or weight per watt, and none notices that the two reviews disagree on the UGREEN's weight by 2.5×. Android Central, CNA, UGREEN UK/US, Native Union and KUXIU could not be read (empty page, fetch blocked, or HTTP 429), so I can't rule out that they have part of this.
decides: It backs the UGREEN on what shoppers worry about most: the laptop still gets 45 W while a phone charges, the same as every rival with a published split, so no one beats it on power. It does not make the UGREEN the travel-weight winner. Verbatim's makers publish 101 g and 105 g, against 135 g or 340 g for the UGREEN, and the page should flag that conflict instead of printing '12 oz; about 6 oz'. A lightest-kit pick would go to Verbatim 30290 only if a US price can be sourced, and right now none can.
